text.title: Django Testing with pytest — Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes one test being written to the rule that decides its shape: DB access mode, client, data construction, mock placement, and the permission matrix.

decision-tree.root-question: Does the test under construction touch the ORM at all?

branch.question: Is it a pure unit test of a util or a serializer's field logic?

branch.conclusion: No django_db marker. Plain pytest function; the pinned settings module is all the Django wiring it needs.
It reaches an external system. Mock at the process boundary only, patched at the USE site, and keep the rest of the call path real.

branch.question: Does the code under test depend on a real COMMIT — transaction.on_commit, a post-commit signal, or raw SQL on its own connection?

branch.conclusion: @pytest.mark.django_db(transaction=True). Accept the truncate cost; this is the only case that earns it.

branch.question: What is being exercised — a service, or an HTTP endpoint?

branch.conclusion: @pytest.mark.django_db (savepoint). Build fixtures from the factory or baker.make; call the real service, never a mocked one.
@pytest.mark.django_db with APIClient + force_authenticate, format='json'. Assert the status, then the body fields (r6-status-and-body-asserts).
One @pytest.mark.parametrize table of (client_fixture, expected_status) instead of N near-identical functions.

text.example: test = POST /api/v1/orders/ as owner, staff and anonymous q-touches-db -> true q-commit-semantics -> false (no on_commit hook) q-surface -> endpoint-role-matrix => r7: one parametrized test over (api_client, 401), (authed_client, 201), (staff_client, 201); fixtures come from the OrderFactory, APIClient + force_authenticate, format='json'.
